LoadedRuleSets.compiled is a public mutable dict defaulting to empty; completeness is only checked at read time by guard_spec, which misses extra or stale entries.
ReferencedByRule variants are three independent optional fields enforced only by a validator; compiler uses `or ""` fallbacks (lines 395, 397, 610, 619).
CompareRule.value is typed Any and an `in` list stays mutable inside the frozen record.
CompiledRule.condition is a mutable sqlglot tree reachable by callers despite the frozen dataclass.

## Code Review Findings

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (5)
<details><summary>5 items</summary>

1. `tests/unit/test_row_rules.py` lines 623-637: `test_an_exception_while_building_or_proving_a_filter_refuses` injects exceptions into `_choose_prefix`, `_rename_ctes`, `_scoped_body`, `_proven_scoped_tables`, `_shape` and `CompiledRule.instantiate`, but not into `_wrapper_body`, `_Scoping.aliases`, `_Scoping.base_index` or the row-rule branch of the `_rewalk` loop. Criterion 16 asks for an exception in each step that builds or proves the filtered derived table. (raised by 1/6 agents)
2. `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` lines 663-699: `LoadedRuleSets.compiled` is a public mutable dict that defaults to empty. A `LoadedRuleSets` built outside `load_rule_sets` can hold row rules with no compiled rule. `guard_spec` catches a missing entry when a request runs, but not an extra or stale entry. (raised by 1/6 agents)
3. `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` lines 271-292: `ReferencedByRule` keeps its two variants as three independent optional fields. Only the `_variant` validator enforces a valid combination. The compiler falls back to `or ""` at lines 395, 397, 610 and 619, so a node built without validation would produce an empty column name instead of failing. (raised by 1/6 agents)
4. `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` lines 204-205: `CompareRule.value` is typed `Any`, and the list held for `in` can still be changed in place inside the frozen record after validation. (raised by 1/6 agents)
5. `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py` lines 522-538: `CompiledRule` is frozen, but its `condition` is a mutable sqlglot tree that callers can reach. `instantiate` copies it, so the current code is safe, but a caller that changes it would alter the shared rule after `prove_compiled_rule` passed. (raised by 1/6 agents)

</details>
